title: Elleni D
content: I was in the operating room having an appendix surgery. I felt like was out of my dark body, as opposed to my light spiritual body. I looked back to see the monitor that showed my heartbeat as a flat, green line. I stood up from the operating table feeling light, free, and free from pain. The room I was in was divided by a border line. Half of the room was where the doctors were. On the other side there were two of the most beautiful nurses I had ever seen. They were calling my name to come to them. I was going to them, stretching out my hands. My left foot was crossing the boundary line. My other foot was just about to cross the line too. Beyond the nurses was like a garden with fresh air and a beautiful smell. There were many children from different parts of the world, but now they called this place home. They were chanting in front of a man dressed in a gown, but I didn’t see his full face. Most of me wanted to go with them, but a small part was listening to the doctors calling me and telling me not to go. I also wanted to see my sister, who was sitting outside and crying. After much hesitation, I said, "In the name of Jesus, I don’t want to go with you," and ran back to the doctors. After I ran and reached the doctors’ side of the room, I felt as if my ear that had gone deaf was punctured. I heard my heartbeat start from the machine beginning to monitor the "beep, beep." Someone kept waking me by hitting my forehead. I was disappointed because she woke me up. I really wanted to go and thought she stopped me from doing that. When I woke up, I felt severe pain in my chest. The 30-minute surgery took longer than they planned. I heard from my mother that the doctor had told her, "Even though the surgery went well, we lost her. It was tough for us." He said to my mom, "Your faith and prayers have brought her back. It was beyond our control."

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: No, Surgery-related, While under general anesthesia, CPR was given (cardiopulmonary resuscitation), Clinical death (cessation of breathing or heart function)
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: More consciousness and alertness than normal, Even though I was in that room, I could see my sister beyond the operation room, the doctors giving up and holding their heads, and the place beyond the line all at the same time. My normal everyday life can't see people beyond walls. It is not multidimensional.
elements.At what time during the experience were: Crossing the line and seeing my sister as I stretched out my hand. Then running back to the doctors after deciding to stay and come back to my body.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Time seemed to go faster or slower than usual
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I have never felt different emotions all at the same time. The experience felt like many experiences at once.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: My hearing had three types: when the doctors called me, I heard a faint sound. When the nurses called me to go home, it was quite loud. When I heard my heartbeat come back, it was so loud to my ears, causing discomfort as it felt like a blocked ear starting to hear.
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, Two of the most beautiful nurses I had ever seen came to take me across the border. Their voices were very calming and reassuring, which was the main reason I wanted to go with them.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: I felt so peaceful as I left my body and started going toward the nurses. I felt sadness when I saw my sister crying and a small part of me also felt sad as I was leaving. It was like a battle of choices, hesitant and torn between the will to go and stay. Finally, I felt disappointed by the anesthesiologist because she woke me up from my journey.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt no longer in conflict with nature
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a definite conscious decision to return to life, Most of me wanted to go to that peaceful place. But I saw my sister crying and wanted to see her the most. My mom was also there, but I longed to return to my sister. Even after waking up, I called her name, wanting to touch her and tell her I didn't leave her and that I love her.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I never thought, even in my beliefs, that we struggle to decide to die. Part of me was afraid to let go, while the rest was convinced to go because it was peaceful.
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, My values changed to embrace people beyond borders and tell them Jesus gave me a second chance to live and share the Gospel more. Life is too short.
elements.Did you seem to encounter a mystical bei: I encountered a definite being, or a voice clearly of mystical or unearthly origin
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, The children were chanting, and the man wearing long robes was called Jesus.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Uncertain, What felt like going to that peaceful place was more comfortable than returning to my painful body.
Yes, Going there meant not returning or seeing my loved ones again.
Yes, The children had life; they lived with Jesus. I saw them in a place like a big house's backyard, where many nurses brought them. They were separated from their loving moms on world maps.
elements.Did you gain information about how to li: Yes, Life beyond is peaceful. The out-of-body experience was calm, with no stress, just perfect peace and lightness.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, Going to Jesus' house felt like being loved, but also like not returning. I saw my sister crying and felt love.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: It was a turning point in my life. I took life seriously and changed, as it was a second chance. When I finally go home to Jesus, I want to show him I have lived purposefully and followed my calling. It wasn't a waste.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, The first part when I moved out of body and how I returned I don't know. But returning felt bad, as I felt all the pain and the hesitation.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Uncertain, I see dreams now that actually happen. It scares me too.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Yes, I heard it in Christian testimonies, but living it is very different. As a kid, I wished to see heaven, but after my own NDE, I don't feel the same.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, I thought it was like a dream, but knew I may have died and returned when my doctors said I slipped away. They said it was a miracle. I realized it wasn't just a dream but a real experience of dying and returning, thanks to Jesus.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, If it was a dream, I would know, but that was different. That's all I understand.
